title: The Fellowship of the Leak: Power Analysis of a Masked FrodoKEM Hardware Accelerator
problem: First-order masked implementations of post-quantum cryptographic schemes like FrodoKEM can be bypassed when masking is only applied to specific operations (matrix multiplication/addition).
motivation: Understanding and improving masking countermeasures is critical for securing quantum-resistant cryptographic hardware against side-channel attacks.
method: The attack measures power consumption from a FrodoKEM hardware implementation (FPGA) using ~10,000 power traces from specially crafted test inputs. Statistical analysis called correlation power analysis identifies patterns in the power measurements that correspond to the secret encryption key. The implementation protects certain operations (matrix multiplication and addition) using random noise masking—one layer of noise protection called first-order masking—but leaves other operations unprotected. By analyzing power leakage from the unprotected operations, the attack recovers secret matrix rows and breaks the encryption.
key_novelty: Incomplete masking allows an attack to break first-order masked FrodoKEM through power analysis when protection doesn't cover all operations.
contributions: Novel first-order side-channel attack bypassing incomplete masking in FrodoKEM
Successful recovery of secret matrix rows using correlation power analysis
Demonstration on Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA with ~10,000 traces
Identification of masking application gaps in post-quantum crypto hardware
limitations: Attack specific to matrix operations; full-system implications not thoroughly analyzed.
primary_theme: Side-channel attacks on masked post-quantum cryptography
